jobs.title: People Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

The People Operations Manager will be responsible for the smooth day-to-day running of Altana’s London office and for supporting the people operations and HR needs of our growing UK team. Working from our London co-working space, this hybrid role blends office and culture management with hands-on people operations — creating a welcoming in-office experience and owning onboarding, benefits, and HR administration for Altana’s UK employees. As Altana expands into Europe, the People Operations Coordinator will also help stand up people operations across new EU locations.

The People Operations Manager will report into Altana’s global People team and will work cross-functionally with Altana’s IT and Finance teams, as well as the UK leadership team.

You Will

- Serve as Altana’s main point of contact with our London co-working/serviced-office provider managing our membership, desks, and meeting-room bookings, and raising any building or facilities issues (reception, cleaning, and facilities are provided by the building).

- Keep the team’s space running smoothly including team supplies, equipment, and any Altana-specific needs beyond what the building provides.

- Own the in-office experience and culture, organise team socials, celebrations, and in-office moments, and run logistics for all-hands, visitors, and events that make the London office somewhere people want to be.

- Coordinate on-site logistics for new joiners and visiting global colleagues and customers, including desk setup, building access, and a smooth first day in the office.

- Own new-hire onboarding for UK employees including offer and contract paperwork, right-to-work checks, inductions, equipment, and first-week setup in partnership with IT and hiring managers.

- Administer UK employee benefits, including enrolment, day-to-day queries, and liaising with providers.

- Manage basic offboarding for UK leavers including exit logistics, equipment return, and access removal (note: this role does not own payroll).

- Support Altana’s expansion into Europe in helping to stand up people operations for new EU locations, including onboarding, benefits, and local HR administration, in partnership with the global People team and external advisors.

- Maintain accurate, up-to-date employee records and support HR compliance and UK (and, over time, EU) employment documentation.

- Act as a first, friendly point of contact for employee questions on benefits, policies, and workplace matters, escalating to the global People team as needed.

- Champion Altana’s culture and employee experience, supporting the global People team on engagement initiatives and people projects.

You Have

- 3-5 years of experience in people/HR operations, office management, or a coordination role, ideally in a fast-growing technology or startup environment.

- Highly organised, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at once.

- Warm, approachable, and service-oriented, you take pride in creating a great workplace and employee experience.

- Genuine enthusiasm for building culture and community in an in-person office environment.

- Sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential and sensitive information.

- Working knowledge of UK employment fundamentals (e.g., right-to-work, statutory leave) and comfort learning HRIS and benefits tools; prior exposure is a plus.

- Interest in or exposure to operating across multiple European markets is a plus, as this role will support our expansion into Europe.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- A proactive, resourceful self-starter who is comfortable working independently and across a global, distributed team.

- Ideally, an interest in our domain and mission.

This is an office-based role in London, with 4–5 days per week in our London office (a co-working / serviced-office space) and occasional flexibility to work from home. Candidates must be within commuting distance of central London.

Salary Range

£70,000 - £80,000

The salary range, to the extent specified for this role, is a good faith statement of the minimum and maximum levels of the annual based salary for the position.  The base salary offered to a successful candidate will depend on a wide range of compensation factors, including, but not limited to, work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. The overall salary package includes a performance-based variable compensation payment paid periodically.  Competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Altana's total compensation package.

Our Values

Our values are the core beliefs that shape who we are, what we stand for, and how we behave.They form the foundation of Altana’s culture and integrity and guide how we hire, design, build, and connect with each other and our customers.

- Trust: Our customers and partners entrust us with missions of the highest importance. We honor that by keeping our word, meeting commitments, and ensuring every action we take reinforces confidence in us. We rely on each other to deliver, to speak openly, and to hold ourselves accountable.

- Resilience: In a world of uncertainty and complexity, our work must withstand challenges, evolve with conditions, and ensure reliability over time. Resilience is both how we operate and what we deliver. It’s how we respond when things don’t go to plan –– we adapt, we support each other, and we keep moving forward.

- Stewardship: We are stewards of every mission we touch. Because our work impacts lives and futures, we hold ourselves accountable to delivering mission impact and never compromising. Our responsibility extends beyond individual projects to the broader system of global trade. We believe that stewardship starts from within so that we can bring focus, creativity, and excellence to our work. Each of us is personally responsible for fostering a workplace where people can thrive. And we are stewards of the greater good of the company. By holding ourselves and each other accountable, we build a culture of innovation and collective success that reflects the scale of our mission.

- Courage: Courage is what unlocks the seemingly impossible for our customers. It’s the core value that drives us make bold moves and take on big, complicated network problems—the ones others avoid. We know success isn't guaranteed, but we have the audacious vision to believe a solution is possible and to build it. Courage fuels our growth mindset. It means embracing challenges that make us stronger, and it’s demonstrated by how we approach hard conversations and complex projects.

At Altana, we believe that a diverse workforce enables greater creativity, performance, and adaptability. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome you to join us as you are. Our employment opportunities and decisions are based on business needs and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, family care or medical leave status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by the laws or regulations in the areas in which we operate. jobs.title: Head of Public Sector Business Development, National Security
jobs.location: Washington, D.C. ; New York, NY ; London, UK
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

Altana's Global Public Sector (GPS) team helps government customers work through hard problems in global trade and supply chains, and it's growing fast. As GPS scales, we're organizing around three domain verticals — Customs & Trade, Resilience & Network, and Policy & National Security — and we're hiring the founding Head of Policy & National Security to grow, manage, and run that business globally.

This is a foundational business development role — a chance to build a business, not just join one. You'll own the growth of Policy & National Security end to end: where the opportunity is, how Altana is positioned to win it, which relationships and contract paths get us there, and the team that makes it happen. Success comes from shaping opportunities early, navigating how the government actually buys, and turning long-term agency bets into won programs — building a durable book of business over time.

You'll be the senior Altana relationship for the agency decision-makers who matter, acting as a thought partner who helps them move through technology transformation. You'll partner closely with the VP of Global Public Sector, Government Affairs, Capture, Product, Delivery and Implementation, Marketing, Finance/Accounting, and executive leadership. For the right operator, this is some of the most ambitious and rewarding work of a career.

You Will

- Own Altana's revenue growth for the Policy & National Security vertical— carry the number, and translate strategy into a concrete plan and a focused set of high-value target agencies.

- Manage a field of sellers and own their pipeline and forecast, pursuing complex, large-scale government opportunities that reflect strategic vision and long-term agency bets — with honest rigor about what's real, what's at risk, and what it will take to land.

- Build and own the Policy & National Security pipeline and forecast, pursuing complex, large-scale government opportunities that reflect strategic vision and long-term agency bets — with honest rigor about what's real, what's at risk, and what it will take to land.

- Shape new opportunities by communicating Altana's value to senior government stakeholders and partnering with them as they design their transformation.

- Develop relationships across agencies, from the operational level to the strategic, and build the trusted standing that keeps opening the next opportunity.

- Own the partner relationships that extend the vertical's reach — systems integrators, primes, teaming partners — activating Altana's broader network to open doors, shape opportunities, and win programs together.

- Work alongside the other GPS leaders to position Altana across the full set of company-wide objectives, so the verticals add up to more than the sum of their parts.

- Anticipate what each pursuit will require and surface those needs internally early, coordinating across teams you don't directly control.

- Feed Policy & National Security signal — budget cycles, policy shifts, competitive intel, real agency needs — into Product, pricing, and company strategy, and own the personas and mission outcomes that help drive the product roadmap.

You Have

- Significant experience in public-sector sales and revenue growth leadership, with a track record of growing the pipeline and the team..

- Deep knowledge of how the public sector actually buys: you've shaped opportunities and made real calls on deal strategies with an understanding of different contracting mechanisms.

- A network across government and industry you can activate, and the credibility to operate at the senior level.

- A builder's instinct: you've led complex efforts, you operate effectively through influence, and you're energized by standing up something new.

- The ability to carry complex, high-intellectual-content software into government; fluency in trade, supply chains, geopolitics, and national security use cases is a strong plus.

- Excellent judgment and communication skills, with the ability to engage senior stakeholders independently and translate complex value into a clear case.

- The patience and optimism to prevail in long government procurement cycles.

- Eligibility to obtain and hold a U.S. Security Clearance.

This role is based in New York, Washington, DC, or London, UK with hybrid work flexibility.

£130,000 - £155,000 GBP

jobs.title: Principal Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

We are looking for a Principal Financial Analyst to serve as the dedicated Finance Business Partner to Altana’s Technology organization — spanning R&D, Implementation, Product, IT, and InfoSec. In this high-impact role, you will be the financial engine that keeps our largest cost center running efficiently and transparently, translating complex technical spend — from cloud infrastructure and AI tooling to headcount and vendor contracts — into clear, board-ready insight. You will sit at the intersection of finance and engineering, partnering daily with senior leaders across the Tech org to drive rigorous budget management, strategic procurement, and performance accountability. This role reports directly to the VP of Finance and is an exceptional opportunity for a data-savvy, technically curious finance professional who thrives in fast-moving environments and wants to build something genuinely best-in-class.

Your Role

- Own the monthly budget forecast, business metrics, and variance reporting for the full Technology organization, delivering timely and accurate financial insight to Tech leadership each period

- Serve as the primary financial advisor to Tech leaders on all investment decisions — building driver-based models, evaluating headcount requests (new hires, backfills, and contractors) against the Board-approved cost envelope, and assessing ad hoc business requests for alignment with approved budget parameters

- Own cloud infrastructure financial management end-to-end: forecast cloud spend across all providers, govern a resource tagging taxonomy for accurate cost attribution, and manage a hybrid commitment discount strategy to optimize cost efficiency

- Build and manage the financial framework for all AI and LLM spend — including token-level unit economics, AI cost attribution by team and product, and monthly reporting on AI spend efficiency versus business outcomes

- Translate cloud and AI infrastructure actuals from billing systems into GAAP-compliant accounting entries, working cross-functionally with Accounting and Cloud Engineering to bridge cloud invoices and the general ledger

- Lead procurement and vendor management for the Tech org: maintain a centralized contract inventory, manage renewal calendars 90–120 days in advance, negotiate cloud and SaaS agreements (ELAs, committed use discounts, renewals), and drive SaaS rationalization by identifying and eliminating overlapping or underutilized tools

- Build and maintain Board-level Technology scorecards tracking performance versus plan — including headcount, cloud and AI spend, R&D as a percentage of revenue, and key delivery indicators — and develop a pod-based financial view to support ROI analysis by engineering pod

- Track and report engineering org ratios (Software Engineer to PM, Software Engineer to Designer) and produce executive financial narratives that connect R&D investment to business outcomes for board presentations, investor materials, and quarterly business reviews

You Have

- 5-8+ years of progressive FP&A or finance business partnering experience at a high-growth technology or SaaS company, with direct experience embedded with R&D, Engineering, or Product organizations; AI company experience is a plus

- Strong financial modeling skills in Excel and at least one EPM/planning platform; SQL proficiency to pull and analyze data independently from a data warehouse is a plus

- Excellent communication and influencing skills: you translate complex financial data into clear executive narratives, engage credibly with engineering and product leaders, and push back constructively on decisions that fall outside approved parameters

- Active and enthusiastic user of AI tools in your day-to-day workflow — for modeling, analysis, automation, or productivity — with a genuine commitment to building AI-augmented finance workflows

- Familiarity with ERP, CRM, and HRIS/workforce planning tools

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA a plus

This role is based in Brooklyn, NY, USA  with hybrid work flexibility and candidates must be within commuting distance from our Williamsburg office.

US Salary Range and Benefits

$170,000 - $200,000 USD
